question: What produces a pleasurable touch when no external cause is possible?
premises: Sometimes no external cause for the touch is possible.
The touch still produces a corresponding pleasurable activity.
That touch can be reflected in some continuum of bodily channels.
inference: When no external cause is possible, one's own reflected touch in the bodily channels produces the pleasurable effect.
uncertainties: nāḍisaṃtatau is read in a general tantric-bodily sense as a continuum of channels.
plain_english: When an external cause is impossible, one's own touch, reflected in some continuum of bodily channels, produces that pleasurable experience.
